key_insight: The survey argues that masked diffusion LLM speedups depend not just on parallel generation, but on specialized inference techniques and a unified way to decompose latency.
engineering_relevance: For deployment, it offers a practical framework to separate algorithmic, architectural, and system bottlenecks so latency improvements can be measured and compared more reliably.
method: Introduces a unified latency decomposition framework for dLLMs
Categorizes acceleration methods into algorithmic, architectural/system, and inference-time scaling axes
Provides benchmarking guidelines for reproducible end-to-end latency evaluation
evidence_signal: The paper is a survey centered on analyzing and comparing inference techniques across real deployments, using latency decomposition rather than a single aggregate benchmark.
watch_item: End-to-end speedups can be misleading if caching, reuse, and system-level overheads are not measured consistently across benchmarks.
paper_title: Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques
